trial_title: PROspective Multicenter Imaging Study for Evaluation of Chest Pain
brief_summary: A prospective multicenter imaging study for evaluation of chest pain. Objective is to determine whether an initial non-invasive anatomic imaging strategy with coronary CT angiography (CTA) will improve clinical outcomes in subjects with symptoms concerning for coronary artery disease relative to an initial functional testing strategy (usual care). eligibility_table.criterion: Known coronary artery disease (CAD) with prior Myocardial infarction (MI), percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) or any angiographic evidence of coronary artery disease (CAD) ≥50% lesion in a major epicardial vessel
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of coronary artery disease with prior CABG, which disqualifies him from this criterion.

eligibility_table.criterion: Any invasive coronary angiography or non-invasive anatomic or functional cardiovascular (CV) test for detection of coronary artery disease (CAD), including coronary tomographic angiography (CTA) and exercise electrocardiogram (ECG), within the previous twelve (12) months
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of invasive procedures related to coronary artery disease, which likely includes tests within the last 12 months.

eligibility_table.criterion: Known significant congenital, valvular (> moderate) or cardiomyopathic process (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or reduced systolic left ventricular function (LVEF) ≤ 40%)) which could explain cardiac symptoms
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has an ejection fraction of 60%, which is above the threshold of 40% for reduced systolic left ventricular function. There is no indication of significant congenital or valvular heart disease.

eligibility_table.criterion: Contraindication to undergoing a coronary tomographic angiography (CTA), including but not limited to: a. Allergy to iodinated contrast agent, b. Unable to receive beta blockers unless heart rate < 65 beats per minute, c. Pregnancy
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about allergies to iodinated contrast agents or the patient's ability to receive beta blockers. Therefore, it is uncertain if there are contraindications for coronary CTA.
